# Rosalind Penrose

## Overview

- **Age:** Forty-five years old (Volume 2), later referenced as nearly forty-six  <sub>[v2 c21 P28](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0028), [v2 c21 P44](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0044), [v2 c23 P11](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0011), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v2 c1 P47](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0047), [v2 c21 P28](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0028)</sub>
- **Status:** Married  <sub>[v2 c25 P30](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0030), [v2 c30 P30](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0030)</sub>
- **Origin:** East Welby / Brierley area  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086), [v2 c22 P10](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0010)</sub>
- **Role:** Homemaker; author/storyteller of imaginative tales to her companion  <sub>[v2 c21 P41](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0041), [v2 c27 P44](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0044)</sub>
- **Titles:** Miss Rosalind  <sub>[v2 c21 P28](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0028), [v2 c21 P62](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0062)</sub>; Mrs. Stephen Stanhope  <sub>[v2 c30 P30](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0030)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** The Queen of the Fir Tree Fairies  <sub>[v2 c23 P6](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0006)</sub>

## Appearance

Rosalind is a tiny woman with snow-white, wavy, and thick hair that she wears in flattering puffs and coils. Beneath her hair, she has a youthful, rosy-cheeked face with sweet lips, large gentle brown eyes with gold flecks, and dimples. She dresses in delicate, youthful clothing, such as cream and forget-me-not organdy dresses with frills, laces, and ribbons.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c22 P10](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0010), [v2 c23 P6](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0006), [v2 c23 P9](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0009), [v2 c27 P53](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0053)_

## Personality

Rosalind possesses an imaginative, romantic, and youthful spirit, defying her actual age through pretending, play, and fancy. Although she considers herself moody and proud—traits that contributed to her past heartbreak—she is deeply affectionate, hospitable, and generous. She treasures beauty, music, flowers, and the company of young people, maintaining a cheerful and humorous disposition despite years of seclusion.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P49](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0049), [v2 c21 P53](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0053), [v2 c23 P11](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0011), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019), [v2 c26 P23](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0023), [v2 c29 P31](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0031)_

## Traits

- Imaginative and fond of pretending  <sub>[v2 c21 P53](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0053)</sub>
- Proud and moody  <sub>[v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)</sub>
- Hospitable and generous  <sub>[v2 c21 P49](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0049), [v2 c21 P64](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0064)</sub>
- Childlike and youthful at heart  <sub>[v2 c23 P8](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0008)</sub>

## Abilities

- Creating imaginative stories and pretend games  <sub>[v2 c27 P44](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0044)</sub>
- Gardening and cultivating flowers, especially lavender and roses  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086), [v2 c27 P22](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0022)</sub>

## Goals

- To keep youth, beauty, and imagination alive in her secluded life  <sub>[v2 c21 P53](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0053), [v2 c23 P8](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0008)</sub>
- To reunite with her long-lost love, Stephen Stanhope  <sub>[v2 c28 P45](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0045)</sub>

## History

Rosalind Penrose resided for decades in the secluded stone residence known as Echo Cottage on the Tory Road near Brierley. In her youth, she was engaged to Stephen Stanhope, but pride and a misunderstanding separated them, leading Stephen to leave for the United States while Rosalind remained unmarried in her ivy-covered cottage. Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke stumbled upon Echo Cottage by accident while taking a wrong path through the woods and quickly befriended Rosalind, charmed by her youthful spirit and imaginative tea parties. Rosalind formed a close bond with Nell and later met Stephen's son, Cedric, whose resemblance to his father deeply moved her. Recognizing the enduring affection between Rosalind and Stephen, Nell facilitated a meeting between them when Stephen returned to visit Brierley. Stephen visited Echo Cottage, where he and Rosalind reconciled after twenty-five years apart. The two were married under the honeysuckle arbor in her garden in late August, surrounded by close friends, and subsequently left to reside in Boston, planning to return to Echo Cottage every summer.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P28](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0028), [v2 c21 P48](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0048), [v2 c23 P18](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0018), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019), [v2 c27 P23](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0023), [v2 c28 P37](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0037), [v2 c28 P64](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0064), [v2 c29 P9](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0009), [v2 c30 P30](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0030), [v2 c30 P33](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0033)_

## Background by volume

- Her father named her Rosalind because of his love for the fragrance of lavender, which he associated with her mother  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- She was engaged twenty-five years prior to Stephen Stanhope, but a misunderstanding and mutual pride broke the engagement  <sub>[v2 c23 P18](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0018), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)</sub>
- She lived in solitude for decades at Echo Cottage with a young hired girl, continually named 'Belinda'  <sub>[v2 c21 P28](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0028), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>

## Quotes

> One requires certain rewards. Occasionally, I doubt I could survive without imagining things.  <sub>[v2 c21 P53](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0053)</sub>

> It feels like a decayed tooth quite a bit... Although you will not consider that a particularly poetic comparison.  <sub>[v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)</sub>

> Everything has simply made me weary... even the reverberations. My existence contains nothing except reverberations... reverberations of vanished expectations, visions, and delights.  <sub>[v2 c27 P34](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0034)</sub>
